title: Appeals and Revision under GST
outcomes: Apply the appeal procedure before the Appellate Authority.
Explain revisional powers and their limits.
Trace appeals to the Tribunal, High Court and Supreme Court.
Compute mandatory pre-deposits and apply monetary limits.

meta.exam_tip: In pre-deposit questions, separate admitted amounts from disputed tax and apply the cap per law.

concepts.title: Appeal to the Appellate Authority
body: An aggrieved person may appeal against an adjudicating authority's order to the Appellate Authority in Form GST APL-01 within 3 months of communication of the order; a further month may be condoned for sufficient cause. The department, through an officer authorised by the Commissioner, may apply within 6 months in Form GST APL-03.

The Appellate Authority hears the appellant, may allow additional grounds where the omission was not wilful, grants at most three adjournments, and may confirm, modify or annul the order. It cannot remand the matter back to the adjudicating authority.

Where the order is likely to increase penalty, fine or confiscation value, or to reduce a refund or ITC, a hearing must be given; a higher tax or wrong ITC demand needs a show cause notice within the time limits of sections 73, 74 or 74A. The authority should try to decide within one year of filing.
concepts.analogy: First appeal within three months, one extra month for cause.
concepts.work: An order communicated on 28 September can be appealed until 28 December.

concepts.title: Revision by the Revisional Authority
body: Under section 108, the Revisional Authority may call for records of a subordinate officer's proceedings, on his own or on information or request from the State Commissioner, and revise an order that is erroneous and prejudicial to revenue, illegal or improper, ignores material facts, or follows an audit observation by the CAG.
Before an adverse order, the person must be given notice and hearing. The authority may enhance, modify or annul the order and can stay its operation meanwhile.

Revision is barred where the order is under appeal, where the appeal time has not expired (or more than 3 years have passed since the order), or where the issue was already revised. Non-appealable orders listed in section 121 are outside both appeal and revision.
concepts.analogy: Revision is the department's internal correction route.
concepts.work: An order ignoring an inward invoice register can be revised within three years.

concepts.title: Appeals to the Tribunal, High Court and Supreme Court
body: Appeals against orders of the Appellate or Revisional Authority go to the GST Appellate Tribunal in Form GST APL-05 within 3 months of communication, condonable by a further 3 months. For orders communicated before 1 April 2026 the backlog window has been notified, with the last date extended to 31 July 2026. The Tribunal may refuse admission where the tax, ITC, fine, fee or penalty involved is ₹50,000 or less.

Appeals from State Benches lie to the High Court within 180 days, but only for appeals raising a substantial legal question, which the court frames and then answers. Orders of the Principal Bench (place of supply issues) go directly to the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court also hears appeals from High Court judgments certified as fit. Interest on refund of pre-deposit runs from the date of payment till refund.
concepts.analogy: Tribunal, then High Court on law, then Supreme Court.
concepts.work: A place of supply dispute decided by the Principal Bench goes straight to the Supreme Court.

concepts.title: Mandatory pre-deposit and monetary limits
body: Before the Appellate Authority, the appellant pays in full the tax, interest, fine, fee and penalty admitted, plus 10% of the remaining tax in dispute, capped at ₹20 crore each for CGST and SGST (₹40 crore for IGST). For a penalty-only order the deposit is 10% of the penalty.
Before the Tribunal a further 10% of the remaining tax in dispute is required, capped at ₹20 crore (₹40 crore IGST). Payment of the pre-deposit stays recovery of the balance.

To reduce litigation, the department files appeals only above monetary limits — ₹20 lakh for the Tribunal, ₹1 crore for the High Court and ₹2 crore for the Supreme Court — subject to listed exceptions such as constitutional validity questions.
concepts.analogy: Pay ten percent to keep the appeal and freeze recovery.
concepts.work: Disputed CGST of ₹84 crore needs a pre-deposit of ₹8.4 crore.

viva.q: Can the Appellate Authority remand a case?
viva.model: The authority must decide the appeal itself by confirming, modifying or annulling; remand power is absent under section 107.
An order erroneous and prejudicial to revenue, illegal or improper, ignoring material facts, or flagged by a CAG observation.

viva.q: What is the effect of paying pre-deposit?
viva.model: Recovery of the balance amount is deemed stayed till the appeal is decided.

viva.q: From when is interest on refund of pre-deposit payable?
viva.model: From the date of payment of the deposit till its refund, at the rate under section 56.

viva.q: When may the Tribunal refuse to admit an appeal?
viva.model: The Tribunal may refuse admission when the tax, ITC, fine, fee or penalty involved is ₹50,000 or less.
